race.office: Governor of Arizona (joint ticket; running mate Lisa Castillo per az-races.json)

nominee.t: Won the July 2026 Green Party primary and is on the ballot under the Green label. The Arizona Green Party disavows her: it voted in May 2026 to actively oppose her, calls her a 'sham' candidate, and on Aug 31 asked the Secretary of State to replace her. That office said it cannot remove a nominee without a court order or her withdrawal (per az-races.json). She did not attend the Oct 6 Clean Elections debate.

ballot.t: She survived two pre-primary ballot challenges (April 2026). A judge found about 40% of her signatures invalid but enough remained (1,771 needed; about 3,250 filed); a second challenge, by Teri Ann Hourihan, was dismissed Apr 13.

oneliner.t: Green Party nominee for governor, disavowed by the Arizona Green Party, who until early 2025 was an elected Republican precinct committeewoman. She is now under Clean Elections Commission and Attorney General investigation over the $5 qualifying contributions that won her about $2.8 million in public funds; no finding or charge has been made.

upbringing.t: By her own account she was born in New York City, moved to Arizona in 1991, raised two daughters who graduated from Peoria schools and ASU, and worked 35 years as a legal secretary/assistant. Maricopa County records reported by the Arizona Mirror show she was a registered Democrat from 2006 to 2016, voted in Republican primaries in 2022 and 2024, and registered Green in 2025. In 2023 she registered T3 Designs, which sold 'Trump Won' and 'Kari Won' buttons and other GOP merchandise.

fec.source: State data — Arizona Clean Elections public funding, as reported by news (seethemoney.az.gov blocked). Not FEC data.
fec.committee: Risa Lombardo gubernatorial campaign (state, Clean Elections-funded)
fec.src_note: About $2.8 million in Clean Elections primary and general funding, released after the Secretary of State certified her 4,000+ $5 qualifying contributions. She stopped spending public funds in July after director Tom Collins's letters; the commission has not ordered a freeze. Pre-funding private fundraising was 'little or none' per KJZZ. The campaign paid Bootstrap Campaigns, a Las Vegas firm formed May 12, 2026 whose original officers were Republican consultants. Collins alleges she failed to report subcontractors O'Neil Printing and Uncle Sam Petitions.

legal.t: The Clean Elections Commission (unanimously, Aug 27, 2026) directed its director to finish investigating whether her campaign actually collected its $5 qualifying contributions. About 74% of 5,000 donor names were shared with two other campaigns; six listed donors told the Arizona Mirror they never gave. The campaign deposited the $5 total in one lump sum on May 4, the day it applied. Collins also alleges two unreported subcontractors. The Attorney General is also investigating (Mirror, Sept 11). Her attorney, Tim La Sota, denies fraud but acknowledged she violated Clean Elections rules by signing forms for contributions she did not personally collect, saying she was confused. Possible outcome: an order to repay up to $2.8M, from personal funds if campaign cash is short.
legal.status: Investigation pending; no commission finding or repayment order and no criminal charge as of Oct 8, 2026. Report due by the Oct 29 meeting. Her suit to block it was dismissed Sept 30 (Judge Melissa Iyer Julian) as premature; Court of Appeals special action pending on an expedited schedule.

research_notes: STATUS NEEDS HUMAN RE-CHECK BEFORE PUBLICATION: Court of Appeals special action (accepted, expedited) and the Clean Elections Oct 29 meeting could change her funding status. As of the latest coverage read (KJZZ Sep 30), there is no repayment order, no disqualification and no charge. She remains on the ballot as the Green nominee; the party's Aug 31 removal request was refused for lack of a court order. 'Sham' is the party's and Collins's characterization, not a finding. DISCREPANCIES: KJZZ quotes La Sota saying the campaigns suspended over fear of repayment; the Mirror (Sep 25) says they stopped spending public funds in July. RELATIVES EXCLUDED: Mike Lombardo (she calls him her ex-husband; the Mirror found no divorce record) is a GOP precinct committeeman involved in the 2020 audit; his record is not hers. Both donated to Josh Barnett's 2024 campaign (Mirror), which is recorded only as reported. Neely (R) and Collier (G) are co-subjects of the probe; their records are not hers. Running mate Lisa Castillo not researched. Site and photo not available.
